newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seen under more pressure Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seen under more pressure Thursday.

text.p: Belgian shares are expected to come under further selling pressure on Thursday, with buyers still absent and the mood cautious ahead of Friday's market holiday when key U.S. monthly jobs data are due.
The Bel-20 index .BFX ended Wednesday 3.35 points or 0.19 percent lower at 1,798.67, near the middle of a 10-point range. Volume was a moderate at 1.7 billion francs.

"We don't see any buyers, but people taking the nice profits made over the last months. That makes for net selling pressure in low volume," one dealer said, "We'll remain like that until the U.S. elections in the middle of next week."
He said the market could benefit from a new-found direction if President Bill Clinton were re-elected and the dollar managed to hold up.
But dollar weakness on Wednesday afternoon hurt U.S.-exposed stocks in particular such as retailer Delhaize, which gets a majority of its turnover from U.S. unit Food Lion.
Delhaize sank 2.2 percent to 1,755 with a hefty 68,159 shares traded.
Utility holding Tractebel was again the most heavily traded stock in value terms, with 21,715 shares changing hands.

The stock ended unchanged at 14,825 francs on the last day of Societe Generale de Belgique's 14,500 a share public offer. SGB made the offer after buying a 25-percent stake in Tractebel from holding company Groupe Bruxelles Lambert.

Volume has been boosted for several weeks by small retail clients taking profits and professionals buying for the put warrant which SGB is offering to dissuade shareholders from actually taking up the public offer.
The put warrant allows shareholders sell Tractebel stock at 14,500 francs in three years' time.
